## Readings for the seat's proposal — managed environment users and the just-in-time default set

Readings-only pass (no closure, no tests, no branch commit). Every reading is taken against **objectstack `6251f5905`** (a detached read worktree) unless it names **objectui `7e9708e`** or the vendor dist **`@better-auth/sso` 1.7.12** (the version `plugin-auth/package.json` pins). The cloud repository is not readable from this account: everything attributed to cloud#3132 or to cloud code comes from the card's quotes or from comments in this tree, and is marked where it matters. The card's line anchors for `ssoOnlyMode` are stale: the code now sits at `auth-manager.ts:7777` (`resolveSsoOnly`), `:1996` and `:7901` (the forced `disableSignUp`) and `:8002` (`features.ssoEnforced`). In this tree a bare `ADR-0024` resolves to the MCP-connectors record; the open mirror of cloud ADR-0024 is **ADR-0135**, so the build cites `cloud ADR-0024` or `ADR-0135`.

### R1 — What a just-in-time user holds today

**Membership.** better-auth's `user.create.after` runs `membershipReconciler` (`auth-manager.ts:8920`). That calls `settleMembership` (`:5060`), which calls `reconcileMembership` (`reconcile-membership.ts:213`). The reconciler yields to any existing `sys_member` row. A host hook, such as the cloud's personal-organization provisioning, chains first (`:8919`). Under policy `auto` and posture `single` it binds the Default Organization with role `member`: `resolveTargetOrg` calls `tenancy.defaultOrgId()`, the "Single-org → default org; multi-org → none (invite/JIT own it)" line at `:5071`. Under `invite-only` or a walled posture it binds nothing. On the `@better-auth/sso` path the vendor also binds the provider's own organization with `organizationProvisioning.defaultRole: 'member'` (`auth-manager.ts:4529`; vendor `assignOrganization`, dist `index.mjs:184–278`). It binds by verified domain only when domain verification is on.

**Explicit grants written: none.** The admission gate classifies a creation as class `provider` (`audience-posture.ts:402–420`) when it arrives through `sso-oidc`, `sso-saml`, or `oauth` on a configured `oidcProviders` id. Per the module doc that includes the cloud platform IdP. `decideAudienceAdmission` answers `{ admit: true, grantPermissionSet: false }` for that class (`:446–450`). No `sys_user_permission_set` row is written for a JIT user. One edge case: under `single`, a JIT user who is the environment's first human able to authenticate is promoted to `admin_full_access` by `bootstrapPlatformAdmin` (header of `plugin-security/src/bootstrap-platform-admin.ts`).

**Implicit baseline: authentication alone, not membership.** It arrives through two channels, and neither reads `sys_member`:
- (1) `SecurityPlugin.resolvePermissionSetsForContextUnmemoized` adds `baselinePermissionSets` whenever `!isAgent && context.userId` (`security-plugin.ts:7112–7196`). The list is `composeHumanBaselinePermissionSets(fallbackPermissionSet)` (`app-default-permission-set.ts:52`): the app's `isDefault` set, which `os serve` passes through `appSecurityPluginOptions(config)` (`serve.ts:4483`), plus `member_default`.
- (2) `resolveUserAuthzGrants` pushes the `everyone` position for every user it resolves (`core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts:1631`). That position's definition names the same baseline plus the package defaults the deployment **accepted**. Under `single` they are accepted through the `sys_audience_binding_suggestion` door (`suggested-audience-bindings.ts`). Under a wall they come from the host option `acceptedDefaultPermissionSets` (`security-plugin.ts:979–1005`).

The SSO wiring's own comment says the same: `member_default` "already grants baseline access to any authenticated user" (`auth-manager.ts:4519–4523`).

**Verdict.** "Arrives with no declared default access" is **literally false of access**. From its first request a JIT user holds `member_default`. It also holds the app's `isDefault` set when the app declares one (on `os serve`), and any everyone-anchor defaults the deployment accepted. The sentence is **true only of declared, JIT-specific, environment-chosen access**: no config key exists for the `provider` class, and nothing is granted per user. A user with no membership holds the sets but sees little: the `_self` carve-outs are keyed on the user, and `sys_organization_self` needs an active organization.

### R2 — The candidate sets (`plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts`)

- **`member_default`** — "Member — Standard Access" (`:582–1120`).
  - No wildcard: the #5491 ruling made it explicit-allow.
  - Read-only on the 28 better-auth-managed tables (`BETTER_AUTH_MANAGED_OBJECTS`, `:61–89`). Several of them still deny through their own declared `_none` default row scope.
  - Five overrides: `sys_user` read and edit on the caller's own row (ADR-0092 whitelist: `name`, `image`, `locale`); `sys_api_key` read and edit on the caller's own keys (`revoked` only); `sys_user_preference` read, create and edit on the caller's own rows; `sys_inbox_message` and `sys_notification_receipt` read.
  - No `allowDelete`, no `allowExport`, no `systemPermissions`, no View/Modify All. It withholds the `Admin` field group of `sys_user`.
  - Row-level security: `owner_only_writes` and `owner_only_deletes` (keyed on `created_by`, `org_member` only); the `_self` carve-outs (organization, own user, org peers select-only, session, two-factor, preference, API key, device code, OAuth consent and application, inbox, notification receipt, invitation self and issuer); `sys_comment_moderation`; the audit-ledger organization scope.
  - It is anchor-safe, and it **is** the baseline (R1). It is the smallest shipped human set, but it is **not read-only**: it carries self-service writes.
- **`viewer_readonly`** — "Viewer — Read-Only" (`:1122–1230`).
  - `'*': allowRead`, plus the managed tables read-only.
  - No write bit anywhere, no `systemPermissions`, no export. Select-only `_self` carve-outs and the audit-ledger scope; it withholds the `Admin` group.
  - It is read-only, but it is the **widest read** of any non-admin shipped set. A wildcard read reaches every non-private object, and under `single` (where Layer 0 is inert) every row in the environment. `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md:205` warns of exactly this.
  - Anchor-safe under ADR-0090 D5 (`spec/src/security/high-privilege.ts:96–100`).
  - No code path grants it. Only the docs mention it: `permission-sets.mdx:173`, "Auditors / read-only stakeholders".
- **The others.**
  - `admin_full_access` is the platform administrator: View/Modify All plus the platform `systemPermissions`. The `selfRegistrationPermissionSet` precedent refuses it.
  - `organization_admin` and `organization_admin_no_bypass` carry `manage_org_users`, `setup.access`, `setup.write` and `manage_mailboxes`, with a wildcard with or without View/Modify All. Both are high-privilege.
  - `mcp_agent_data_read`, `mcp_agent_data_write` and `mcp_agent_restricted` are agent ceilings. The ADR-0090 note puts them on an explicit denylist for persons: "an agent ceiling is not a person's set".

**Reading.** No shipped set is both the smallest and read-only. The smallest human set is `member_default`, which every JIT user already holds. The only read-only human set is `viewer_readonly`, which is the widest read. "The smallest read-only platform set" therefore names nothing that exists as written.

### R3 — The just-in-time path

**Paths that create an IdP-provisioned user:**
- (a) **genericOAuth on an `oidcProviders` entry** (`auth-manager.ts:4296–4316`). This covers the cloud platform IdP (`objectstack-cloud`) and a customer's OIDC configured statically. better-auth's `handleOAuthUserInfo` calls `internalAdapter.createUser`. That runs `user.validateUserInfo` (`source.method: 'oauth'` plus the providerId), then `user.create.before` and `user.create.after`, then `account.create.after`. The last one runs `stampIdentitySource`, which sets `sys_user.source = idp_provisioned` (`:9089`).
- (b) **`@better-auth/sso` OIDC and SAML** (`sys_sso_provider`, `OS_SSO_ENABLED`; `:4497–4533`). The same creation chain runs, with `sso-oidc` or `sso-saml`. Then the vendor runs `provisionUser`, which is not configured here. The vendor calls it on registration, or on every login with `provisionUserOnEveryLogin` (dist `index.mjs:3104`, `:4053`). After that comes `assignOrganizationFromProvider`, and a `/callback/` after-hook runs `assignOrganizationByDomain` (domain verification only).
- (c) **SCIM `POST /Users`** is class `operator`. It is not a first entry, and no session is created.
- (d) **Social providers** (Google and similar) are class `self-serve`, gated by the posture. They are not IdP-provisioned in the operator sense.

**First entry of an existing user.** `session.create.before` settles membership only for a user created in the same request (ADR-0093 D7; `usersCreatedInRequest`, `auth-manager.ts:5106`). Nothing is re-decided at sign-in. Linking an account to an existing user is not a creation either.

**The single place a default would be granted.**
- The admission gate `validateAudienceAdmission` (`auth-manager.ts:5300`) is the one seam that holds `source.method`. It judges only `source.action === 'create-user'`. It stages the grant (`stageSelfRegistrationGrant`, `:5952`, keyed by lowercased email).
- `user.create.after` lands it (`settleSelfRegistrationGrant`, `:5990`). The grant is owned by the first membership's organization, or persisted as a claim that settles on the first `sys_member` row (ADR-0131 D3).
- Today only `self-serve` reaches this path (`grantPermissionSet: true` under `email_domain` or `open`). If the `provider` arm answers `grantPermissionSet: true` when a JIT set is declared, it reuses all of this machinery. That includes `selfRegistrationSetResolvable` (`:5775`; fails closed with `AUTH_CONFIG_ERROR`) and the idempotent `landSelfRegistrationGrant` (`:6036`).
- **Once, at creation — not on every entry.** The vendor's `provisionUserOnEveryLogin` is unused and would cover path (b) only.

### R4 — The config key's spelling

**Conventions.** The audience declaration has three layers that mirror each other:
- **Spec:** `AuthConfigSchema.audience` = `AudienceConfigSchema` {`posture`, `allowedEmailDomains`, `selfRegistrationPermissionSet`} (`spec/src/system/auth-config.zod.ts:399–520`). Its superRefine refuses inert keys (ADR-0078).
- **Runtime twin:** `resolveAudience` and `assertAudienceConfig` (`plugin-auth/src/audience-posture.ts:141`, `:232`). They run at construction (`auth-manager.ts:1720`) and on every merged `applyConfigPatch` (`:4963`).
- **Settings namespace `auth`:** keys `audience_posture`, `audience_allowed_email_domains` and `audience_self_registration_permission_set` (`service-settings/src/manifests/auth.manifest.ts:104–136`, plus four translation files). `bindAuthSettings` binds them (`auth-plugin.ts:2157–2280`). The settings service derives an `OS_AUTH_*` override for every manifest key (`OS_AUTH_AUDIENCE_POSTURE` and so on).

Two keys differ. `ssoOnlyMode` lives in the spec (`:614`), in plugin config, and in a hand-read env var `OS_AUTH_SSO_ONLY` (`auth-manager.ts:368`), with no settings key. `membership_policy` is a settings key plus `OS_AUTH_MEMBERSHIP_POLICY`. On `os serve` the stack's own `auth.audience` is **not** passed to the auto-composed AuthPlugin (`serve.ts:4248–4300`). There it is reached through the settings/env door, and a host that constructs AuthPlugin itself (the cloud factory) passes options.

**Where the key belongs.** It belongs in the audience declaration, "the ONE declaration answering who may become a user". Its sibling already names the set a self-registrant receives, and the JIT set is the `provider`-class twin of that sibling. Each candidate below is declared in the same homes: the spec's `AudienceConfigSchema`; plugin-auth's `audience-posture.ts` (`ResolvedAudience`, `resolveAudience`, `assertAudienceConfig`, `decideAudienceAdmission`); `audienceKeys` in `auth-plugin.ts`; and `auth.manifest.ts` with its translations.
1. **`audience.enterpriseSsoPermissionSet`** / `auth.audience_enterprise_sso_permission_set` (derived env `OS_AUTH_AUDIENCE_ENTERPRISE_SSO_PERMISSION_SET`). It matches the console copy ("enterprise SSO … admitted under every posture") and the module doc, and it excludes social providers by name.
2. **`audience.providerPermissionSet`** / `auth.audience_provider_permission_set`. It matches the code's class name. The trap: to an author, a Google sign-up reads as "provider", but that sign-up is `self-serve`.
3. **`audience.jitPermissionSet`** / `auth.audience_jit_permission_set`. It is the card's word. The trap: social-provider OAuth is also just-in-time, and this key does not cover it.

Unlike its sibling, the key is legal under every posture, because provider JIT is admitted under `invite_only`. So the sibling's "refused for invite_only" rule does not carry over. The `admin_full_access` refusal does.

### R5 — `isManaged()`

**What exists today.**
- `isHostKernelComposition(plugins)` (`core/src/stack-auth.ts:112–118`) asks for the name `com.objectstack.runtime.objectos-environment` or the class `ObjectOSEnvironmentPlugin`.
- Two places read it: rule 3 of `resolvePlatformAuthComposition` (`host-kernel`), and serve's own inline copy `isRuntimeHostKernel` (`serve.ts:3925–3928`), which is a second spelling of the same predicate.
- The plugin itself is not in this repository. It belongs to the cloud's `createObjectOSStack`, multi-tenant branch only.
- **Control-plane binding:** `CloudConnectionPlugin.start()` computes a local `platformManaged = (controlPlaneApiKey ?? OS_CLOUD_API_KEY) !== ''` (`cloud-connection-plugin.ts:316–335`; ruling 甲 on #25097, which produces 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` refusals). It is not exported.
- No managed-mode spelling exists: `git grep` for `OS_CLOUD_MANAGED|cloud_managed|cloudManaged|isManaged(` hits only the local `isManaged(object)` in `identity-write-guard.ts`.

**The structural catch.** On the hosted shape, `ObjectOSEnvironmentPlugin` sits on the **host** kernel, which is a routing shell with no AuthPlugin. Every judgement site this card names runs on the **per-environment** kernel that the cloud's `ArtifactKernelFactory` builds (`serve.ts:4146–4163`; `plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts:146`). That kernel's plugin list carries no `ObjectOSEnvironmentPlugin`, so `isHostKernelComposition` cannot be asked where the answer is needed. Separately, the single-environment `objectos-ee` shape wires no `ObjectOSEnvironmentPlugin` (`serve.ts:1990–1997`).

**Narrowest home.** The narrowest home is `@objectstack/core`, beside `isHostKernelComposition` (lane `domain:engine`). plugin-auth, cli and cloud-connection all depend on core. The accessor would hold a process-level fact that the boot establishes once (host composition **and** bound control plane), and every kernel in the process reads it. It honours the dev/test override only on a development boot or a test rig. Note that `isDevelopmentBoot` alone excludes vitest, which sets `NODE_ENV=test`. The name should be `isCloudManaged()` rather than `isManaged()`: "managed" already names `idp_provisioned` identities (ADR-0135 D2/D4), `managedBy` tables and `managed_by` provenance. The alternatives are in open question 2.

**`features.sso` today.** `AuthManager.getPublicConfig()` builds `features` (`auth-manager.ts:7968–8019`: `sso` at `:7998`, `ssoEnforced` at `:8002`, `audiencePosture` at `:7984`), and the `/auth/config` route refines it (`auth-plugin.ts:2798–2812`). A new flag must be classified in `PUBLIC_AUTH_FEATURES` (`spec/src/kernel/public-auth-features.ts`), because the drift guard `plugin-auth/src/public-feature-registry.test.ts` asserts that served booleans equal the registry. It may also be declared on `AuthFeaturesConfigSchema` (`spec/src/api/auth-endpoints.zod.ts:227`, which declares `ssoEnforced` but not `sso`). Every key in that object is camelCase.

**Production refusal.** It goes in `os serve`, beside the ADR-0131 boot refusals (`serve.ts:4667–4685`: `const productionBoot = !isDev; … throw new Error(…)`, before any plugin starts). The accessor must also ignore the variable outside dev/test, because embedded kernels (`createStandaloneStack`, verify's `bootStack`) and the cloud's per-environment kernels never pass through serve.

### R6 — The audience posture

**Values.** `AUDIENCE_POSTURES = ['invite_only','email_domain','open']` (`spec auth-config.zod.ts:362`), default `invite_only`. `audiencePermitsSelfRegistration` is true for both `email_domain` and `open`.

**How it is read.** Everything reads it through `AuthManager.getAudience()`, which calls `resolveAudience(this.config.audience)` (`:4998`):
- **The admission gate.** Under `invite_only` it refuses a self-serve creation with 403 `SELF_REGISTRATION_CLOSED`, unless a pending, unexpired `sys_invitation` or the bootstrap window admits it. The `operator` and `provider` classes are never gated.
- **Forced email verification.**
- **`features.audiencePosture`.**

**Card nuance.** "Refuses `open`" has to mean "refuses every posture but `invite_only`". `email_domain` also opens self-registration, and the maintainer's word covers self-registration in the app in general.

**The door.** `assertAudienceConfig(raw, emailAndPassword, options)` (`audience-posture.ts:232`) runs in two places. At construction (`auth-manager.ts:1720`) a refusal stops the boot. On every merged `applyConfigPatch` (`:4963–4967`) the standing config keeps ruling. On the settings path, `bindAuthSettings` (`auth-plugin.ts:2228–2276`) logs "[auth] audience settings REFUSED — the standing posture … keeps ruling" at `error`.

**Existing error vocabulary.** Entry refusals throw a plain `Error`, "[audience] invalid audience configuration: …", with no wire code. The admission codes are `SELF_REGISTRATION_CLOSED`, `EMAIL_DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED` and `AUTH_CONFIG_ERROR` (constant `AUDIENCE_CONFIG_ERROR`; `audience-posture.ts:103–107`). A managed arm is one more `fail(…)` branch keyed on the accessor, with no new code. The settings select (`auth.manifest.ts:104–117`) cannot read the mode, so the refusal is the enforcement.

**Sign-up is a second door.** `invite_only` still admits a self-serve sign-up that holds a pending local `sys_invitation`. Under `ssoOnlyMode`, `disableSignUp` is forced true (`auth-manager.ts:1996`, `:7901`). "No local sign-up" under the managed mode therefore means forcing the same two arms on the accessor and refusing local invitation creation (R7).

### R7 — Setup → Users, server side

**Server doors.** plugin-auth mounts all of them, and none consults `ssoOnlyMode` today. `git grep` finds only the `disableSignUp` arms and the public config.
1. **Invitation creation:** `organizationHooks.beforeCreateInvitation` (`auth-manager.ts:3750`). It is the one seam behind `POST /organization/invite-member`, which the four invite actions call: `sys_user` `invite_user` (`sys-user.object.ts:83–118`), `sys_member` (`:104`), `sys_invitation` resend (`:65`, `:112`), and the `sys_organization` page. `sys_invitation` is better-auth-managed, so the generic data path already fails closed (ADR-0092). `git grep` finds no other insert into `sys_invitation` in plugin-auth.
2. **`POST /admin/create-user`** (`auth-plugin.ts:3172`, `runAdminCreateUser`) mints a local `env_native` account.
3. **`POST /admin/import-users`** (`auth-plugin.ts:3442`, `runAdminImportUsers`) creates local identities. Its `invite` policy sends an account-invitation password-reset email.
4. **`POST /admin/set-user-password`** (`auth-plugin.ts:3423`) is offered today to platform admins on **every** row (`sys-user.object.ts:301–315`, no `source` predicate).
5. **`POST /set-initial-password`** (`auth-plugin.ts:2860`) lets any session holder without a credential mint a local password. This is by design: it "lets a user that the platform onboarded via the objectstack-cloud OAuth provider sign in with email/password". Its header names a twin in the cloud's `AuthProxyPlugin`, which this repository cannot see.
6. The better-auth native `/request-password-reset`, `/reset-password` and `/change-password` are not refusal candidates: break-glass needs them.

**Refusal precedent.** cloud-connection's platform-managed doors answer 409 `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` with a message naming the platform (`cloud-connection-plugin.ts:199–205`). No new error code is needed.

**UI-only.** Display only; no door reads these. They are the `visible` predicates on the platform-objects actions (`invite_user` ×4, `create_user`, `set_user_password`; lane `domain:engine`) and the console. ADR-0135 D5.2 already splits `change_my_password`, `change_my_email`, `delete_my_account` and `set_user_manager` by `record.source != "idp_provisioned"`.

**The objectui half (objectui `7e9708e`):**
- `packages/auth/src/types.ts`: the `AuthFeatures` type needs the new flag.
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx`: `identityImportEnabled = isIdentityImport && features?.admin === true && isAdmin` (`:1936`) gates the import wizard that posts `/admin/import-users`. This is also where a "where to invite" line on the Users list would render.
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/identityImport.ts` and `IdentityImportPanels.tsx`.
- `packages/app-shell/src/console/organizations/manage/MembersPage.tsx` (Invite member button `:159–167`, dialog `:312`), `InviteMemberDialog.tsx`, `orgCapabilities.ts`.
- `packages/app-shell/src/console/home/RecoveryPasswordReminder.tsx` (with `recoveryReminderGate.ts`) nudges every SSO user to set a local recovery password.
- `packages/auth/src/LoginForm.tsx` already consumes `ssoEnforced`.
- `packages/i18n/src/locales/*.ts` for the new line.

### R8 — Break-glass

**No break-glass flag exists. Break-glass is a population:** users who hold a local `credential` account (`sys_account.provider_id = 'credential'`). `stampIdentitySource` keeps those users at `sys_user.source = env_native` (`auth-manager.ts:9089–9133`). Gaining a credential flips `idp_provisioned` back to `env_native`, "so the break-glass admin never loses self-service password management".

**Guards.**
- `isLastLocalCredentialHolder` (`last-local-credential.ts:53`) on `/delete-user`, `/admin/remove-user` (`auth-manager.ts:2646–2735`) and `/admin/ban-user` (`admin-ban-endpoints.ts:166`), answering 409 `LAST_LOCAL_CREDENTIAL`.
- `registerLastAdminGuard` (`last-admin-guard.ts:908`, wired at `auth-plugin.ts:1695`): no write may leave zero administrators able to sign in, in any context.

**What "stays editable" means.** ADR-0135 D5.2, mirroring cloud ADR-0024 D5.2, splits the surface by the D2/D4 population, "not switched off wholesale". It names `set-initial-password` and the admin `set_user_password` as the break-glass routes. So every narrowing must key on `source` or the credential, never switch the surface off wholesale.
